preamble: Each across solution contains the letters of a tree, not necessarily consecutively but always in the correct order. These are ignored in the subsidiary part of the clues.

clue.text: Rapidly calculating for a short time — long time's a failure

parts.note: T is the standard short form of time
an era is a long period of time
a flop is a failure, as of a show that closes early

explanation.surface: Someone sums up a brief spell of trying, and a long one, as a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A teraflop is a unit of computer speed, a trillion floating-point operations per second, so it describes rapid calculating.

clue.text: Resurrection of old poem by chieftain

indicators.note: a resurrection raises something up, and in a down entry raising the word turns it bottom to top

parts.note: rime is the old spelling of rhyme, a poem, as in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner

explanation.surface: A tribal leader brings an ancient poem back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or commander, a chieftain of his people.

definitions.meaning: someone who works like a ... is a dogged, reliable worker
the wooden horse of Troy, hence also the name of a disguised computer virus

explanation.definitionFit: Working 'like a Trojan' means working hard and loyally, and the Trojan horse is the famous wooden ruse.

clue.text: Exposed to drugs, having reclined outside

indicators.note: the reclining word is placed outside, wrapping round the drugs

parts.note: lain is the past participle of lie, so having reclined means having lain
dope is slang for drugs

explanation.surface: Someone lying back is vulnerable to narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid open means exposed or left vulnerable, as to criticism or attack.

clue.text: People like Cassandra's emotional state raised by mystery author

indicators.note: in a down entry raising a word reads it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a mood is an emotional state
Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective mysteries

explanation.surface: A prophetess's frame of mind is lifted by reading a crime novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra foretold disasters no one believed, the model for prophets of gloom.

clue.text: Well-known top and tail of a mouse

indicators.note: to top and tail is to cut off both ends, so only the inside of the run of words that follows is kept

explanation.surface: A celebrated rodent is described from head to tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Run 'of a mouse' together and cut off its first and last letters; what is left sits inside those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous is a straight synonym for well-known or celebrated.

parts.note: the first letter of the tree birch, which the preamble says the clue ignores

indicators.note: half of the word is taken, here its first three letters

parts.note: Henry Esmond is the hero of Thackeray's novel The History of Henry Esmond
the rest of the tree birch, ignored by the clue as the preamble says

explanation.surface: Part of a fictional hero is buried in new earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is BIRCH; its letters are ignored by the wordplay, which gives only ESM, the first half of ESMOND.
explanation.definitionFit: To besmirch is to soil or sully, literally or a reputation.

clue.text: Colour up in bed for the time of your life

indicators.note: the reversed colouring word goes inside the bed

parts.note: hay makes a bed, as in to hit the hay

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: to dye is to colour

explanation.surface: Blushing between the sheets marks someone's finest hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A heyday is a period of greatest success or vigour, one's prime.

clue.text: Article, the right thing to wear

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the first letter of the tree oak, ignored by the clue as the preamble says
the rest of the tree oak, ignored by the clue as the preamble says

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing is just the job for the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is OAK; its letters are ignored, so the wordplay gives only AN and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket, an article of clothing.

parts.note: the first letter of the tree fir, ignored by the clue as the preamble says
a means one, as in a pound
the rest of the tree fir, ignored by the clue as the preamble says

explanation.surface: Only a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is FIR; once it is set aside, 'one' supplies only the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and just both mean even-handed and impartial.

parts.note: joy is happiness
A means first, as in A1 or grade A
the damson, a plum tree, whose letters the preamble says the clue ignores

explanation.surface: Someone who writes about animals puts joy before everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is DAMSON; the wordplay gives only JOY and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy Adamson wrote Born Free, about raising the lioness Elsa in Kenya.

parts.note: the first three letters of the sloe, the blackthorn tree, ignored by the clue
the last letter of the sloe tree, ignored by the clue as the preamble says

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tiny gap lets in an untidy person.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is SLOE, the blackthorn; the wordplay gives only V and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloven is a slovenly, untidy person, which is what a scruff is.

clue.text: Accurate translation from Ovid cures one

indicators.note: a translation renders the words into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Reading the Latin poet in English heals someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Veridicous is a rare word for truthful, telling things accurately.

parts.note: the start of the apple tree, ignored by the clue as the preamble says
in a Guardian crossword the paper calls itself us
the last letter of the apple tree, ignored by the clue

explanation.surface: A newspaper is greeted with acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is APPLE; ignore its letters and only A and US remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause is clapping and cheers, the noise of approval.

indicators.note: off describes the word as going wrong, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the first letter of the tree ash, which the clue ignores; it falls among the scrambled letters
the rest of the tree ash, ignored by the clue as the preamble says

explanation.surface: Daylight robbery takes place near a petrol pump.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is ASH; the clue itself only scrambles RIP into PRI, and the tree's A happens to fall between its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Parish-pump affairs are local ones, the pump standing at the centre of a village parish, so a parish is the district round it.

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor
a beef is a complaint

explanation.surface: A seaman grumbles about the rations aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt beef, beef preserved in brine, was the traditional ration aboard ship.

parts.note: ans is the usual abbreviation for answer, a solution
the elm tree, whose letters the preamble says the clue ignores

explanation.surface: A senior churchman offers the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is ELM; only ANS comes from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: St Anselm was Archbishop of Canterbury under William II and Henry I.

clue.text: Pretend to be sick and remain undergraduate

indicators.note: in a down entry the staying word sits beneath the degree

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
to linger is to remain

explanation.surface: A student stays at college by faking illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's single word 'undergraduate' must be read as two, 'under' and 'graduate', for the down placement to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to feign illness to avoid work.

clue.text: Gypsies raised on a pound, which is unprincipled

indicators.note: in a down entry raising reads a word from the bottom

parts.note: Roma are the Romani people
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Travellers lift a sum of money in a way that lacks morals.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means lacking any moral principles.

parts.note: the first letter of the plum tree, ignored by the clue as the preamble says
the end is the final part
a U-bend, the shape of the letter, is a bend
the rest of the plum tree, ignored by the clue as the preamble says

explanation.surface: A clock is set at the last turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is PLUM; only END and U come from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendulum regulates a clock, so it is the timekeeping part.

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
hoes are garden tools for weeding

explanation.surface: Urban gardening tools keep coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoes are repeats of sound, or things that repeat earlier ones.

clue.text: Scottish personality not in high fashion

parts.note: the start of the bay tree, ignored by the clue as the preamble says
sel is Scots for self, one's own personality
the last letter of the bay tree, ignored by the clue

explanation.surface: A Scottish celebrity is out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is BAY; the clue gives only SEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Basely means meanly, in a low way, the opposite of acting nobly or loftily.

indicators.note: the thin word holds the line inside it

parts.note: bony means thin
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A slim mountaineer clings to the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Bryony is a climbing hedgerow plant.

clue.text: Rock musician gets a dollar, first to last

parts.note: the start of the cherry tree, ignored by the clue as the preamble says

indicators.note: the first letter moves to the end of the word

parts.note: a buck is slang for a dollar
the rest of the cherry tree, ignored by the clue as the preamble says

explanation.surface: A guitarist is paid a dollar, initially and finally.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is CHERRY; the wordplay gives only UCKB.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuck Berry was an American rock and roll guitarist and singer.

parts.note: the start of the may tree, the hawthorn, ignored by the clue
the last letter of the may tree, ignored by the clue as the preamble says

explanation.surface: A label and a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is MAY, the hawthorn; only N comes from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Many means a large number, as in a good many.

definitions.meaning: the fallen nuts of beech and other forest trees, used as pig feed
the upright spar that carries a ship's sails

explanation.definitionFit: Mast is both beechnuts as forage and the pole rising from a ship's deck.
